extra.message: Insecure Deserialization (pickle) in acct_bundle_thaw_174 — Remote code execution — full server compromise by crafting a malicious pickle payload [verified: acct_bundle_thaw_174: duplicate of idx 1; pickle.loads() on line 62 on user-supplied bytes enables arbitrary code execution during deserialization.]

Server-Side Template Injection (Jinja2) in acct_jinja_cast_488 — Remote code execution via Jinja2 template expression injection — full server compromise [verified: acct_jinja_cast_488: duplicate of idx 2; user-controlled `fragment` concatenated into Jinja2 template on line 124 then rendered, enabling SSTI-to-RCE.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write in acct_dock_shelf_494 — Arbitrary file write on the server. Overwriting Django source files, settings, or templates leads to remote code execution or persistent backdoor. [verified: acct_dock_shelf_494: duplicate of idx 3; unsanitized `name` param on line 131 enables path traversal for arbitrary file write with request body content.]

OS Command Injection in acct_shell_probe_506 — Remote code execution as the web server user — full server compromise, data exfiltration, lateral movement [verified: acct_shell_probe_506: duplicate of idx 0; user-controlled `host` reaches os.system() on line 139 with no shell-escaping. _wrk_gate() only authenticates, does not sanitize.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 — Remote code execution on the server via Jinja2 sandbox escape, or sensitive data extraction from Django settings and environment variables. [verified: acct_jinja_cast_488: user-controlled `fragment` param concatenated into Jinja2 template string on line 124 then rendered; allows arbitrary template expression injection.]

Arbitrary File Write via Path Traversal — Arbitrary file write on the server. An attacker can overwrite application code (e.g., Django views, settings), inject a Python module, or write to system directories, achieving remote code execution. [verified: acct_dock_shelf_494: user-controlled `name` param used in Path join with BASE_EXPORT_DIR on line 131 and request body written to file; `../` traversal allows writing anywhere on filesystem.]

OS Command Injection via unsanitized host parameter — Remote code execution on the server as the Django process user, leading to full system compromise, data exfiltration, and lateral movement. [verified: acct_shell_probe_506: user-controlled `host` param flows directly into os.system() shell command on line 139; no sanitization or shell-escaping applied. _wrk_gate() is auth-only, not a sanitization control.]

Hardcoded Weak Default Django SECRET_KEY — An attacker who knows the default SECRET_KEY can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, password reset tokens, and any signed data, leading to complete account takeover and privilege escalation. [verified: settings.py:6 uses `SECRET_KEY = os.getenv("DJANGO_SECRET_KEY", "dev-only-change-me")` — a weak, guessable fallback. If DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset (e.g., production misconfiguration), an attacker knowing this default can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens, achieving full account takeover.]

Default Django SECRET_KEY in Production — Session forgery, CSRF token prediction, password-reset token forgery. Complete account takeover of any user, including platform admins. [verified: Same root cause as idx 0/3: SECRET_KEY defaults to "dev-only-change-me" when the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is absent, enabling session forgery, CSRF token prediction, and password-reset token forgery.]

Path Traversal with PII Exposure in acct_vault_stash_239 — Arbitrary file write of attacker-controlled PII (SSN, credit card numbers) to any path — sensitive data persistence and potential server compromise [verified: acct_vault_stash_239: duplicate of idx 4; `../` traversal via `ref` param on line 78 writes .json files to arbitrary directories with SSN/card data.]

Missing Authentication on acct_identity_ping_337 — Any anonymous attacker can reach this internal ops endpoint — information disclosure and a foothold for further attacks on the ops surface [verified: acct_identity_ping_337: duplicate of idx 8; no _wrk_gate() call on line 91, allowing anonymous access to an internal ops endpoint.]

Missing Authentication Gate on ops Endpoint — Unauthenticated anonymous access to an internal ops endpoint. The endpoint reflects user input, potentially enabling information gathering or further attacks. [verified: acct_identity_ping_337: completely lacks the _wrk_gate() gate check (line 91); any anonymous user can reach this ops endpoint and supply arbitrary handle/channel values.]

Permissive CORS with Credentials in acct_origin_mirror_466 — Any external website can make credentialed requests to the internal ops endpoints — enables cross-origin data theft and state-changing operations [verified: acct_origin_mirror_466: duplicate of idx 7; Origin header reflected into ACAO with credentials=true on lines 108-109; any origin can make credentialed cross-origin requests.]

Permissive CORS with Origin Reflection — Any malicious website can make credentialed requests to the CRM API on behalf of authenticated users, enabling data theft, CSRF-style attacks, and session hijacking. [verified: acct_origin_mirror_466: Origin request header reflected into ACAO header with Allow-Credentials: true on lines 108-109; any external site can make credentialed cross-origin requests.]

Debug Mode Enabled by Default — Detailed error pages expose file paths, environment variables, database configuration, and source code snippets to unauthenticated users when exceptions occur. [verified: settings.py:7 has `DEBUG = os.getenv("DJANGO_DEBUG", "1") == "1"` — DEBUG defaults to True when the env var is absent, causing Django debug error pages to leak stack traces, file paths, environment variables, and source snippets to unauthenticated users.]

DEBUG Mode Enabled by Default — Information disclosure of internal source code, environment variables, database queries, and application secrets via Django debug error pages. Aids attackers in reconnaissance. [verified: Same root cause as idx 1/4: DEBUG defaults to True when DJANGO_DEBUG is unset, leaking detailed error tracebacks and configuration to unauthenticated requesters.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints — Unlimited brute-force attacks on user passwords and password-reset tokens. Account takeover through credential guessing. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware, DRF throttling, or decorator is configured anywhere in the project. Login (LoginView), password-reset (PasswordResetView), and contact_invite endpoints accept unlimited authentication attempts, enabling brute-force credential guessing and password-reset token enumeration.]

Missing rate limiting on login and password-reset endpoints — Unlimited brute-force of user passwords and unlimited password-reset email generation, enabling account takeover and denial-of-service via inbox flooding. [verified: Neither LoginView (urls.py:9), PasswordResetView (urls.py:11), nor any middleware configures rate limiting; zero matches for ratelimit/throttle/django-axes across the entire codebase. All demo users share the known password DemoPass123! (seed_demo.py:12), enabling unlimited brute-force of credentials and password-reset email flooding.]

Disabled user bypass in can_manage_org — 11 views allow management actions for disabled accounts — An admin who disables a rogue account manager expecting to lock them out fails: the disabled user can continue to modify organizations, manage API keys, upload documents, create deals, and invite contacts. Full integrity and confidentiality compromise of managed organizations. [verified: can_manage_org at authz.py:46 never calls ensure_enabled(user), so a Profile.disabled=True user retains a valid session and can still modify orgs, manage API keys, upload documents, create deals, and invite contacts via the 12 views that rely solely on can_manage_org for authorization. No middleware or other guard covers this gap.]

Hardcoded Default Password in contact_invite — Unauthorized access to newly created customer accounts — anyone knowing the contact email can log in with the default password [verified: Same hardcoded-password issue as finding [0]; contact_invite sets all invited users' passwords to 'DemoPass123!' and discloses it in messages (line 197≈199). Repeat of [0] at a slightly different line reference.]

Information Disclosure via Debug Error Response — Server filesystem path leaked in error responses — aids path-traversal and reconnaissance [verified: account_memo_ping_031: duplicate of idx 11; RuntimeError message on line 33 exposes BASE_EXPORT_DIR path in JSON error response on line 35.]

Sensitive Credentials Written to Application Logs — Exposure of authorization tokens/credentials in log files — enables session hijacking or credential theft [verified: account_casefeed_roll_032: duplicate of idx 6; Authorization header and request body logged in plaintext on line 35 with no redaction.]

Open Redirect in account_wayback_card_033 — Phishing — an attacker can redirect users from the trusted domain to a malicious site after the gate check passes [verified: account_wayback_card_033: duplicate of idx 5; unvalidated `lane` param passed to redirect() on line 42 enables open redirect to arbitrary external URLs.]

Weak PRNG for Security Token Generation — Security tokens generated with a predictable PRNG can be guessed by an attacker who observes outputs [verified: acct_nonce_roll_516: duplicate of idx 13; uses random.choice() for token generation on line 146 instead of cryptographically secure secrets module.]

Internal Path and Configuration Disclosure in acct_trace_panel_536 — Attackers learn the absolute server path and Django settings module — enables targeted path traversal and recon [verified: acct_trace_panel_536: duplicate of idx 10; leaks DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR path in JSON response on line 159.]

Weak Predictable PRNG for Nonce Generation — Nonce values generated by this endpoint are predictable, enabling an attacker to forge authentication tokens or bypass anti-replay protections that depend on these nonces. [verified: acct_nonce_roll_516: uses random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) for token generation on line 146, not the cryptographically secure secrets module.]

Information Disclosure of Internal File Paths and Env Vars — Reveals filesystem structure (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) and Django configuration details, aiding attackers in reconnaissance for further exploitation. [verified: acct_trace_panel_536: returns DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR path in JSON response (line 159); leaks internal filesystem path and config module name.]

Missing Secure Flag on Session and CSRF Cookies — Session hijacking over unencrypted connections. An attacker on the same network can intercept cookies transmitted over HTTP and impersonate authenticated users. [verified: Neither SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE nor CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE is configured in settings.py; both default to False. Without the Secure flag, session and CSRF cookies are transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, enabling session hijacking via network-level eavesdropping (MITM).]

Missing Secure and HttpOnly flags on session and CSRF cookies — Attacker on the same network (coffee-shop Wi-Fi, compromised router, malicious ISP) can intercept session cookies in plain HTTP traffic and hijack any authenticated session. Any XSS flaw anywhere in the app becomes a CSRF bypass vector because the CSRF token is readable by JavaScript. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are absent (default False, Secure flag missing — valid). However, SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY defaults to True in Django 5.2 (not False as claimed), and CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=False is intentional Django design for AJAX support. The genuine Secure-flag omission allows cookie interception over HTTP.]

Unrestricted file upload with no content-type validation — Authenticated attacker can upload arbitrary file types to the media directory, enabling stored XSS (via .html files served to other users) or potential remote code execution (if the web server processes .py/.exe/.php from the media path). [verified: Same vulnerability as idx 0 — DocumentForm.clean_file() lacks any content-type/extension/magic-byte validation. The reported line 37 is inaccurate but the unrestricted file upload claim holds.]

Unrestricted File Upload — No Content-Type or Extension Validation — Attacker can upload executable files, HTML with XSS, or other arbitrary content to the media directory [verified: DocumentForm.clean_file() (forms.py:78-83) validates only file size (5MB), not content type, extension, or magic bytes. Files served via direct media URL with content-type from extension enable stored XSS (e.g., .html uploads) from authenticated platform_admin/account_manager users.]

Webhook Secret Stored in Plaintext in Database — Database access reveals plaintext webhook signing secrets — enables forging webhook deliveries to external systems [verified: Same vulnerability as finding [0] — Webhook.secret stored in plaintext at line 192. No encryption or hashing is applied, so database access reveals webhook signing secrets usable for forging deliveries to third-party systems.]

Webhook Secret Stored in Plaintext — An attacker with database read access can obtain webhook secrets to forge webhook events, impersonate the CRM, and potentially pivot to connected third-party services. [verified: Webhook.secret (CharField, line 192) stores the raw signing secret without hashing, unlike ApiKey which uses secret_hash. Anyone with DB read access (SQLi, admin panel, backup) obtains plaintext webhook secrets usable to forge events to external services.]

Escalation queue reveals other agents' escalation metadata to support agents — Support agents can enumerate all escalation titles, severity, and status across their visible orgs, learning sensitive information about cases they are not assigned to (customer issues, internal priorities, business processes). [verified: escalation_queue filters by visible_orgs() but NOT by assigned_agent. A support agent with one escalation in an org sees ALL escalation titles/severities/statuses in that org. escalation_detail properly restricts per-esc, but the queue leaks cross-agent metadata.]

CSV Formula Injection in Data Exports — Arbitrary code execution on the computers of users who open exported CSV files in spreadsheet applications. An attacker can set organization/deal names to formula payloads like `=CMD|'/C calc'!A0` or `=HYPERLINK(...)`. [verified: Customer contacts can set escalation titles (escalation_create) that are written verbatim to CSV export via csv.writer() with no formula-character sanitization (export_csv, kind='escalations'). A title like '=HYPERLINK(...)' executes when opened in a spreadsheet.]

Denial of service via unbounded CSV import file size — An authenticated user can upload a multi-gigabyte CSV file to exhaust server memory, causing application crash or unavailability. [verified: import_data at operations/views.py:501 calls uploaded.read() with no file-size validation; DocumentForm.clean_file in forms.py:68 proves a 5 MB limit is intentional elsewhere, but none is applied here, and no global DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE is set in settings.py. An authenticated account_manager or platform_admin can exhaust server memory via a large CSV.]

Weak MD5 Cryptographic Hash — Provides an MD5 hashing oracle and uses a cryptographically broken hash function. Minimal direct impact in isolation, but contributes to overall cryptographic weakness. [verified: acct_digest_fold_277: uses hashlib.md5() on line 97; MD5 is cryptographically broken, though this endpoint only provides a hashing oracle with limited direct impact.]

User Enumeration via Different HTTP Status Codes — An attacker can enumerate which handles/identifiers are valid in the system by observing the different HTTP status codes (404 vs 403). [verified: acct_identity_hint_456: returns HTTP 404 for unknown handle vs 403 for wrong verifier (lines 117-118); allows probing which of the two hardcoded handles exist.]

Security Headers Disabled in acct_frame_slip_476 — Increased susceptibility to XSS and clickjacking attacks. Users visiting this endpoint in a browser lose CSP and XSS-filter protections. [verified: acct_frame_slip_476: duplicate of idx 9; X-XSS-Protection disabled and CSP set to empty on lines 117-118; removes browser defenses though endpoint serves static JSON.]

Security Headers Explicitly Disabled — Removal of XSS protection and CSP headers makes the endpoint more vulnerable to XSS attacks. Combined with other vulnerabilities, this amplifies the impact. [verified: acct_frame_slip_476: explicitly disables X-XSS-Protection and sets empty CSP on lines 117-118, removing defense-in-depth headers; response is static JSON so impact is limited.]

Disabled SSL Certificate Verification in acct_trust_drift_546 — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept and modify the outbound HTTPS connection — data tampering and credential theft [verified: acct_trust_drift_546: duplicate of idx 15; ssl._create_unverified_context() on line 168 disables TLS verification; URL is hardcoded so exploitation requires DNS compromise.]

Disabled TLS Certificate Verification — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS connections from this endpoint. An attacker on the network can intercept and modify the response from the target server without detection. [verified: acct_trust_drift_546: creates unverified SSL context on line 168 for HTTPS connection; URL is hardcoded to partner.invalid so MITM requires DNS compromise or code change.]

API Key Secret Exposed in Django Messages — The one-time API key secret persists in session storage and may appear in server logs, browser storage, or be exposed to other middleware, defeating the one-time display security guarantee. [verified: api_key_create (line 387) stores the one-time API key secret in Django messages (session-backed by default), persisting it past the intended single-display window. No custom logging middleware exists, but the session-persistence slightly defeats the one-time guarantee.]

Client-Controlled Access Elevation in acct_badge_gate_526 — Any attacker who knows the `lead` badge value gains elevated access to payroll and casework data [verified: acct_badge_gate_526: authorization decision on line 152 based on client-supplied cookie/header value; no downstream consumer shown, but the pattern is a broken access control anti-pattern.]

Client-Controlled Authorization Bypass in acct_badge_gate_526 — Privilege escalation within the ops console. Any request with the correct cookie/header value gains elevated access regardless of the actual authenticated identity. [verified: acct_badge_gate_526: duplicate of idx 28; client-supplied badge value on line 152 determines authorization response; privilege claim is cosmetic with no downstream consumer.]
